Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Unchecked desire obscures pure consciousness to varying degrees, just as smoke covers fire, dust covers a mirror, or the womb covers an embryo.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding how desire obscures self-awareness and distorts perception.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna uses three vivid analogies to explain degrees of cognitive distortion: smoke covering fire (mild/human stage), dust covering a mirror (moderate/animal stage), and womb covering an embryo (deep/vegetative stage).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns that internal awareness exists across a spectrum and can be uncovered through purification.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Degrees of Cognitive Obscuration: Varying levels of mental clouding caused by emotional reactivity
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Self-Awareness Spectrum: The range of awareness from total unawareness to full clarity
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Cleansing Perception: Clearing away mental distortion to restore objective perception

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dhumenavriyate vahnir (As fire is covered by smoke—slight covering)
Yathadarso malena ca (As a mirror is covered by dust—moderate covering)
Yatholbenavrto garbhas (As an embryo is covered by the womb—dense covering)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Self-knowledge is covered by lust in different intensities, illustrated by fire covered by smoke, a mirror covered by dust, or an embryo enclosed in the womb.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Emotional clouding happens in stages. Just as a dusty mirror cannot reflect clearly, a mind clouded by intense cravings loses its ability to see situations accurately. Cleaning the mind restores clarity.
